community: Remote & backcountry, Columbia Shuswap Regional District

description.value: Hamber Park is a vast remote wilderness in BC's Kootenay region, forming part of one of the world's largest contiguous protected area blocks and designated a UNESCO Canadian Rocky Mountains World Heritage Site. Access to the interior requires a 22 km journey from the Sunwapta Falls trailhead in Jasper National Park, with the primary destination being Fortress Lake and its surrounding alpine terrain. Facilities are minimal by design: a rustic campground with a toilet exists at the east end of the lake, while the rest of the park is undeveloped backcountry.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The BC Parks website confirms Hamber Park is an active wilderness protected area and UNESCO World Heritage Site, with a rustic campground that includes a toilet. The website explicitly states 'potable water is not available in the park,' ruling out water refill. No cycling infrastructure, bike parking, or cycling-specific activities are mentioned; access is via a 22 km wilderness hiking trail from a Jasper National Park parking lot, suggesting this is not a practical stop for road or gravel touring cyclists.

enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Hamber Park is a legitimate and notable attraction (UNESCO World Heritage Site) but is a remote wilderness with no road access, no cycling infrastructure, and access only via a 22 km wilderness trail through Jasper National Park — making it unsuitable as a practical cycling tourism service stop. It could be relevant as a bikepacking destination if trail cycling is permitted, but no evidence of that exists in the available content.
enrichment_extras.notes: The air-accessed commercial fishing camp on Chisel Creek Fan is the only quasi-commercial facility noted in the park, but it is not described as offering services to general visitors beyond boat rental.

blurb: Roadless UNESCO wilderness park around Fortress Lake, reached by a 22 km hike from Jasper.
